notes:
Summary: Lost in procurement to Fireworks (decision 2026-03-02). Competitive win attributed to pricing for burst capacity and existing partner discount. Internal ops lead who sponsored POC left during evaluation — lost momentum and champion. Security team flagged HSM/KMS integration timeline as a blocker; Fireworks committed to a roadmap that met their timeline.

Timeline / activities:
- 2026-01-20: Initial intro; proven interest in private deployment + dedicated GPUs. AE: Liam Ortiz. SE intro: Priya Nair.
- 2026-01-25: Discovery call (ff-cerb-20260125-01) — workload: high-throughput customer chat + personalization, strict residency.
- 2026-02-08: Shared pricing model and cost projection (drive: rfp). Estimated infra delta vs current: ~25% lower on Redwood when quantized. Prospect asked for dedicated burst pricing comparison.
- 2026-02-18: Demo + POC kickoff (ff-cerb-20260218-demo). POC focused on latency SLO (p95 < 120ms) and embedding throughput (5k reqs/min).
- 2026-02-25: POC interim: Redwood met latency targets but cost per 1M tokens higher under their predicted load pattern; engineering noted need for custom batching config.
- 2026-02-28: Security review submitted (SEC-1872). They require SSO/SAML, audit logging, KMS with HSM-backed keys, and 7-year retention policy for logs — extra compliance ask.
- 2026-03-01: Internal sponsor (Ops Lead, "Jordan Hale") left the company; decision window compressed.
- 2026-03-02: Final procurement meeting — procurement selected Fireworks citing better bundling for burst capacity and pre-approved partner discounts.

Key quotes / signals:
- "Fireworks gave us a clearer path to HSM integration within quarter — that's the timeline we need." (Head of Security)
- "We can't reopen budget this quarter; decision is final." (Procurement)

Why we lost (post-mortem):
- Pricing: Fireworks' burst/pool pricing made a stronger unit-economics case for their multi-tenant offering at our expected spike patterns.
- Timing & roadmap: Security needed HSM integration timeline that matched their quarter; they perceived Fireworks' roadmap as more closely aligned.
- Champion attrition: sponsor left — no internal advocate to push overdue approvals.
- Procurement relationship: Fireworks had an existing reseller/partner agreement with the customer's SI vendor.

Open follow-ups (for revival):
- Send formal bow-out email and 1-pager describing where Redwood differentiates on reliability & cost controls.
- Request detailed procurement feedback / win-loss survey (owner: Liam).
- Target re-engage: 2026-09 (after new fiscal planning). Offer to run a cost-sensitivity micro-POC focusing on batch/caching to show NRR improvements.

Attachments / refs: pricing deck (drive link), POC logs (drive link), security spreadsheet (attached SEC-1872).
